h1. Scenario 2: (changing *CANCEL* decisions to *FINISH*)

looking at the *cancel scenario*, the bad decisions would be the ones where the ride happens and the driver reaches out to CS, where Bolt would need to compensate the trip back to their balance. 

for July and August, we had:

* 15k cancelled rides per month
* 5.3% were compensated back

checking how many minutes the rider tries to cancel the active order, we can find a threshold:

* if we decide to *finish* the ride instead of *cancel* if the request happens at least 10min after the ride started, we’ll:
** 22.5% were compensated back
** we’ll cover 42% of the bad cases
** we’ll at MAX affect 10% of the cancellation requests that are currently being cancelled 
** 21.5k cost saving per month 

important to remember that finishing the ride doesn’t necessarily mean the rider will be charged. a price review can still happen and the Pricing system can still not charge/overcharge the customer. so finishing the ride, doesn’t mean we’ll be creating a problem for the rider. for the driver’s side, it’s a better experience. they get paid, and we save CS and compensation costs for Bolt. 

*new rule created*:  [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/rules/edit/ridehailing_user_cancel_ongoing_ride_check/LONG_ACTIVE_ORDER_FINISH?configTab=config_view&tab=basic|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/rules/edit/ridehailing_user_cancel_ongoing_ride_check/LONG_ACTIVE_ORDER_FINISH?configTab=config_view&tab=basic]

If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

o.id,
CONCAT (CONCAT (CONCAT ('https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/', CAST(o.id AS varchar)), '/' ), CAST(o.city_id AS varchar)) AS orderlink,
o.city_id,
o.country,
o.created, 
o.user_id, 
ot.driver_id,
o.payment_method_type,
o.state, 
ot.state,
ot.client_cancel_reason,
ot.reject_reason,
o.TYPE,
o.campaign_code,
cb.campaign_id,
cb.id, 
cb.created,
sat.id, sat.external_id, sat.external_id_namespace, sat.reason, sat.created, sat.state, sat.target_user_id, sat.source_amount, sat.source_currency, sat.target_amount, sat.target_currency, sat.country_code
FROM ng_public.company_order AS o 
JOIN ng_public.company_order_try AS ot ON ot.order_id = o.id AND ot.city_id = o.city_id AND ot.retry_to_try IS NULL AND ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date) as date)
LEFT JOIN ng_public.rider_conditional_campaign_bonus AS cb ON cb.order_id = o.id AND cb.city_id = o.city_id AND cb.user_id = o.user_id AND cb.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date) as date)
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_balance_user.balance_user_service_account_transfer AS sat ON sat.external_id = cb.bonus_id AND sat.target_user_id = o.user_id
WHERE o.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -2, current_date) as date) 
AND o.TYPE = 'scheduled'
AND o.state = 'no_driver_provided'
AND o.id IN (1230760510,1230684052)
AND o.city_id = 18
LIMIT 15 {code}

despite the very high bad ratio, we need to worry more about false positives here. because if we change from *deny* to *cancel*, we’ll cancel orders that are getting finished and we lose GMV. 

check these examples:

[https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/530938522|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/530938522]
[https://ukraine-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1102336718|https://ukraine-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1102336718]
[https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1227236130|https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1227236130]
[https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/526501040|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/526501040]

all of these are good trips that happened where the rider tried to cancel the ride in the 1st minutes after it was started. my assumption is that either the driver started these trips too early or the rider got trigger-happy and tried something shady. point is, if we allow these orders to be canceled, we won’t get their GMV. 

33% of the rides we denied the cancellation ended up with price 0 anyway, so no harm was done to the users, except for the fact that maybe we lost GMV from the ride that they wanted to do and sought another option when they couldn’t get a Bolt driver.

the decision here is about: 

* 47k of good GMV from false positives vs 21k refunded per month
* lost business from riders that don’t get the service they wanted

considering we don't get too many escalations about issues around this scenario, I’m leaning towards leaving as it is.

LightHouse Team has provided a short memorandum analyzing the registration requirements for us when the the Cyber and Data Protection Regulations, 2022 (“Draft Regulations”) published in November 2022 enters into force.

*To comply with this law we will have to:*

* get a data protection license as a data controller
* Appoint the DPO

*To get a data protection license we have to:*

* complete a self-assessment using the licensing eligibility tool available on the Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Zimbabwe's (POTRAZ) website ([https://www.potraz.gov.zw/|https://www.potraz.gov.zw/|smart-link] )
* complete and file the Data Controller Self-Assessment FORM DP1 (see FIRST SCHEDULE PART I of the Draft Regulations [https://www.potraz.gov.zw/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Draft-Cyber-and-Data-Protection-Regulations-.pdf|https://www.potraz.gov.zw/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Draft-Cyber-and-Data-Protection-Regulations-.pdf])

Then if we are eligible for licensing we have *to apply for data protection license* and for this to:

* complete and file the Data Controller Application FORM DP2 (see FIRST SCHEDULE PART II of the Draft Regulations)

*Appoint the DPO*

* complete and file the DPO DESIGNATION/APPOINTMENT NOTIFICATION FORM DP3 (see THIRD SCHEDULE of the Draft Regulation)
* DPO is required to undergo a certification course offered (within three months of the coming into effect of this regulations) → even though the Draft Regulations does not specifically say anything about the DPO being present onsite, I believe that requirement can mean that (need still to confirm this bit).

 

*Nest steps:*

Based on:

# the information posted on the regulator’s website: [https://www.potraz.gov.zw/?page_id=2220|https://www.potraz.gov.zw/?page_id=2220|smart-link] where only the Draft Cyber and Data Protection Regulations is posted
# latest news featured on Data Guidance is about the Draft Cyber and Data Protection Regulations
I can confirm that the *Cyber and Data Protection Regulations, 2022 (“Draft Regulations”) published in November 2022 has not been adopted yet.*

Thus in the meantime in terms of next steps I agree with the The LightHouse Team that they will be more of a “prep“ nature and will include:

# completing the self - assessment form on the website ;

# preparing drafts of all the forms and

# monitoring official updates to determine once the Regulations come into effect.

This obligation stems from the [Data Protection Act 5 of 2021|http://www.potraz.gov.zw/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Data-Protection-Act-5-of-2021.pdf] which is currently force . As mentioned on [Slack|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07CLNASN5V/p1726594736014559], I think the language in the global process (i.e., what to escalate to Privacy) could be revised to the following:

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
"_Include the following information for review by Privacy:_

* _The Beehive case Link(s)_
* _The estimated date/time that the incident occurred_
* _Details of how the incident occurred (in particular how did the third party gain access to the driver's account?)_
* _The incident's current status and whether it has been resolved (i.e., the steps taken in response and whether the driver has regained ownership of the account)_
* _Any negative effects of the incident (i.e., were any unlawful changes made to the account, and/or has the driver suffered any financial detriment? If so, have these issues been remediated?)_"
{panel}

Some key reasons behind this are as follows:

* We ideally need to know the method used by a scammer to gain access to a user’s account. This is because, for regulatory reporting purposes, we need to be able to group incidents by the methods used.
* It is crucial that we understand whether the driver has suffered financial detriment, as this substantially increases the risk profile and may affect whether we need to fulfil certain reporting obligations on the privacy side.

In short, if the above details are not included by CS when the initially escalate the case the Privacy, it is highly likely that we would ask these questions as a preliminary step. As such, it would save some time on both sides if this information were included from the get-go.

Happy to discuss 🙂

Update here: the integration logic is working exactly as expected. The issue has been functionally, that historically we have always been pulling the *full* PO amounts, as we have not had “partial invoices”. This is a functional problem statement, rather than integration.

In order to resolve this, the following functional changes have been done in SBX, tested and passed:

On report, the following two fields have been problematic: 

* Quantity
* Extended Amount

This was pulling the full Purchase Order amount, even though that we have had an invoice against it.

Therefore, those two fields are being replaced with the following:

* Quantity > Remaining Quantity
* Extended Amount > Remaining Extended Amount

The web service alias will stay the same meaning no integration changes required here.

We now add a new Customer Contact option on the Maps to prompt when you add a contact type row on the *Maintain Contact Types* task.



!image-20240919-105657.png|width=554,height=323,alt="image-20240919-105657.png"!

Note: You can't remove the contact type row if it's in use.

Workday now enables you to select contact types on the Contact Type prompt when you add or edit customer contacts on the Addresses and Contacts tab on a customer profile. 

!image-20240919-110039.png|width=1406,height=343,alt="image-20240919-110039.png"!

Workday also displays the *Contact Type* column with the contact type information for contacts that have the contact type specified. 

Note: You must have active customer contact types on the Maintain Contact Types task for Workday to display the prompt and column on the customer profile.

* *Put Business Entity Contact Web Service*

Workday updates the *Put Business Entity Contact* web service to support active customer contact types available on the *Maintain Contact Types* task when you add or update customer contacts using this web service. 

Note: You can add a business entity contact for contact types set only for customer usage when you create:

* Customers.

Please let me know if you have any questions. 
Cheers, 
Marten

This is a legal requirement, and it has nothing to do with Bolt

Hello,

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.
For issues with refunds from Beehive, kindly reach out to #beehive-agent-support on Slack.

Hello,

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

If by criteria you mean how are they flagged: 

*Ride too short block* 

- Those are flagged by central ops, via a looker. Only the top offenders are flagged. For more information you can contact Martin Farmakov.



Looker: [https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/13682?Timeframe+Picker=Date&Created+Week=2023%2F10%2F23+to+2023%2F10%2F31|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/13682?Timeframe+Picker=Date&Created+Week=2023%2F10%2F23+to+2023%2F10%2F31]

*Client did not show*

- A looker is run to check drivers that have more than 14 orders in which the client didn't showed, in a timeframe of 14 days. 

Then you do a ratio in between the number of finished rides and the ones in which the client didn't showed. 

If its ratio is equal or superior to 0.8, the driver is flagged


Looker: [https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/looks/25058?toggle=fil|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/looks/25058?toggle=fil]

*Rider cancellations:* 

We want to tackle drivers that accept a ride, and then go away from the pickup point.

For this, a looker is run in which: 

- eta must be under 7 minutes, and *Orders Client Cancelled Before Driver Arrived* must be equal or above than 14. 

Then a correlation between finished orders and those is made, and if the value of rides cancelled by the rider is superior to 15%, the driver is flagged. 

Looker: 

[https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/looks/25841?toggle=dat,fil,pik,vis&qid=oJZgT7FO8CaCKBrdNz8vK3|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/looks/25841?toggle=dat,fil,pik,vis&qid=oJZgT7FO8CaCKBrdNz8vK3]

* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

[https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/optimizer-hints|https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/optimizer-hints|smart-link] 

Optimizer hints are case insensitive and specified within {{/*+ ... */}} comments following the {{SELECT}}, {{INSERT}}, {{UPDATE}} or {{DELETE}} keyword in a SQL statement.

Multiple hints can be specified by separating with commas. For example, the following query uses three different hints:

{noformat}SELECT /*+ USE_INDEX(t1, idx1), HASH_AGG(), HASH_JOIN(t1) */ count(*) FROM t t1, t t2 WHERE t1.a = t2.b;
{noformat}

How optimizer hints affect query execution plans can be observed in the output of {{EXPLAIN}} and {{EXPLAIN ANALYZE}}.

An incorrect or incomplete hint will not result in a statement error. This is because hints are intended to have only a _hint_ (suggestion) semantic to query execution. Similarly, TiDB will at most return a warning if a hint is not applicable.



See *_Troubleshoot common issues that hints do not take effect_* section:

[https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/optimizer-hints#troubleshoot-common-issues-that-hints-do-not-take-effect|https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/optimizer-hints#troubleshoot-common-issues-that-hints-do-not-take-effect|smart-link] 

Most likely, during the incident, the hint was misplaced. We can verify it by checking the modified queries and warnings on their execution.

_Clause 17.1 - Delivery drivers must check in at the main Site office on arrival for instructions on where to safely unload or load Goods, and must wear safety gear such as helmets and high-visibility vests. Drivers must stay with their vehicle if traffic management details are provided._
_Clause 17.2 - Hazardous materials must come with a safety data sheet under the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations (COSHH). This sheet should detail safe handling, storage, and emergency procedures, and the materials must be properly labelled following the Chemicals (Hazard Information Packaging for Supply) Regulations._
_Clause 17.3 - Each delivery must include information on how to safely handle, use, install, store, and maintain the Goods. A risk assessment and method statement must be approved before offloading._
_Clause 17.4 - Deliveries and loading must meet Department of Transport (DfT) UK standards. Drivers must have all required documents and follow Site rules._
_Clause 17.5 - Risk assessments and loading/unloading plans must be provided before delivery. Drivers must carry certification proving their competence, such as CPCS or ALLMI, and check with Lovell if unsure._

_Clause 17.7 - To supply recycled Goods, Bolt must be REACH registered. Without proof of this registration, Lovell may reject the Goods without liability._

_Clause 19.1: If Bolt supplies or makes goods from waste, they must follow Lovell’s WRAP Quality Protocol, or Lovell can reject the goods without penalty. Bolt is responsible for getting and following this protocol._

_Clause 19.3: Polystyrene packaging is generally banned unless agreed upon in advance; if used, Bolt  must handle its removal._

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

Problem analysis:
From the profile, it can be confirmed that within the ten minutes when the problem lasted, the largest resource consumption was reading the CLUSTER_SLOW_QUERY table, which would read the slow log file. Since a large number of slow logs were generated on the faulty node, the resource consumption was large. As for why a large number of slow logs were generated, the more likely reason is that one undiscovered large query causing some SQL to slow down and be recorded in the slow log, this creates a vicious cycle when combined with slow log reading. But because the large query was not completed, it was not recorded in the tidb log.
Until we get proof, this is just a reasonable guess.Here are some suggested actions:
Adjustments you can make now:
changed log.level of all tidb-servers to “warn” or “info” : [log] level = “warn”
reduce the slow log file size from 300 to 100 : [log.file] max-size = 100
one-minute profile before and when the problem occurs is needed. So continue profiling is still useful. Please enabled and keep it for 3 days (if you can find the problem immediately and export the profile, you can keep it for 1 day)
turn on TOP SQL, which will show the high-consumption SQL being executed, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/v7.1/top-sql#enable-top-sql
If it happens again next time, spend 2 minutes collecting the following data before stop server,  for further investigation:
Profile when the problem occurs: Before shutting down , manually collect a 60s profile, refer to https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/v7.1/dashboard-profiling
Profile before problem occurs: continue profiling can provide this
Clinic: It can provide more logs than last time, especially expensive queries that take more than 60s
TOP SQL: view the statement and sql plan which has the highest CPU usage on the problem node
restart tidb-server at last (delete the slow log file of the node for faster recovery)

** The temporary investigative block is placed on the reported user’s account when the matter is being investigated. This is a safety measure so the alleged bad actor cannot commit any more misconduct when using Bolt services.
** The consequential block is a result of an investigation, and in a way, it resembles a punishment for the reported user. It could be a 1-day block, 3-day block, 7-day block or even a permanent hard block. Based on the Event Confirmation and Occurrence, the Tool will suggest a consequential action for the reported user based on the Global Blocking Matrix. *What we do:*

# We do keep deleted card details in our systems. I have checked this for this user as well.
# We keep only last 4 digits of the card, card expiry date, card scheme - visa or master card, date the card was added and deleted.
# We do not store full card details in our systems without unmasking, eg in case of any unauthorised access to the database, the illegitimate users would not be able to unmask the card until the get an encryption key or would not be able to get access to the card with only 4 last digits.
# We do not delete the details of the card as we do not have retention policy in place.



*What I propose:*

# Inform the user that we do keep the details about the deleted cards in our systems, but they are not accessible from the Bolt App.
# Inform that we keep only last 4 digits of the card, card expiry date, card scheme and date when the card was added and deleted.

# As we do not have a purpose why we keep this data and the user did not ask it in the initial letter, we can omit providing the purpose in the fist response. If the user gets back, I propose we rely on the following purpose- *To investigate and respond to claims and disputes relating to the use of Bolt services.*

*Proposed solution*:

Upon receiving an RnA request approval, admin-access-request will check if the approver can also approve the other RnA request connected to the root admin access request (e.g. admin-access-request receives approval of a manager request, and the manager is also one of the role/permission owners eligible to approve the owner request or the other way around). If the approver is eligible to approve the other connected RnA request, admin-access-request will:

* Consider the root admin access request fully approved.
* Cancel the other RnA request in RnA with a comment like: Request no longer needed, the source admin access request already approved by user XYZ.
* If cancelling the other RnA request fails, the automation stops and we’re back to the regular scenario.

(/)  The mechanism will only work for “singleton” requests, i.e. requests for only a single role/permission. For compound requests, the “approval extension” is tricky, because I could be owner of two requested permissions, and I can be willing to approve only one and not the other, so I wouldn’t want my approval of one of the permissions to be extended to the other.

⛔  The mechanism will not work for requests with This request is on behalf of multiple users, because those are a bit tricky in the first place, as they need approval from the requester’s manager, while logically IMO, they should need approvals from the managers of the users about to receive a new permission/role.

(/)  The mechanism will work for singleton Update Roles requests (i.e. adding exactly one permission to exactly one role) if the permission owner is also the role owner.

*Impact analysis:*
I’ve checked the last 1k access requests for each type, and here are the results:

{noformat}Permission requests:
    84% are singleton requests
    1.3% of singleton requests are eligible

Role update requests:
    75.7% are singleton requests
    9.4% of singleton requests are eligible

Role requests:
    79.3% are singleton requests
    25.4% of singleton requests are eligible{noformat}

It actually makes sense that _some_ roles are team-specific, and then it’s probably not that rare that the team’s manager is also the role owner.

h3. Role-Based Security Reporting

Workday continues to improve how you audit role-based security, making it easier for you to view role-based security access for workers and role assigners, and to build custom reports.

*Posted: 2024-06-17 Updated: 2024-09-18 Release 2024R1*

Impact: Interface Change Setup Effort: Automatically Available

Business Benefits

This helps you easily identify when a worker has had their role-based security access granted, revoked or had no security impact, and for what reason. You can also identify when the staffing transaction has been rescinded or corrected, and for what reason.

Changes

We deliver a new *Role-Based Security Audit* report (secured to the _Customer Central Security Administration_ and _Security Administration_ domains). You can use the report to view role-based security access for workers, role assigners and constrained role-based security groups for these staffing transactions:

* Hire
* Job Change
* Termination

Workday assigns:

* Security granted status when you assign a worker to a position using 1 of these staffing transactions and the position has current or future-dated role assignments.
* Security revoked status when workers move out of a position with existing role assignments.

For changes to constrained role-based security groups, Workday creates an entry for security group changes that impact the role assignment.

We deliver a new *Role-Based Security Audit Log Lite* report data source (RDS) (secured to the _Customer Central Security Administration_ and _Security Administration_ domains) that you can use in custom reporting to identify workers with granted or revoked role-based security. We also deliver these new report fields on the new *Role Based Security Audit Log Lite* business object (secured to the _Customer Central Security Administration_ and _Security Administration_ domains):

* Security Effective as of
* Security Change Reason
* Security Change Reason Details
* Security Outcome
* Assignable Role
* Security Groups
* Role Assigner
* Role Assignee
* Initiator
* Completed By
* Transaction Processed
* Transaction

We deliver the new Worker report field on the new Role Based Security Audit Log Lite business object (secured to the _Worker Data: Public Worker Reports_ domain).

h1. Concept: Formula Writer and Explainer

The Worksheets Formula Writer generates a workbook formula based on your description of what you want the formula to do. You can insert the resulting formula into the workbook, or you can use the generated formula as a guide and make edits to it. You need edit access to the workbook to use the Formula Writer.

h2. Generative AI and How Worksheets Uses It

Generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) encompasses a range of AI systems that create many kinds of content. Worksheets uses a generative AI model when generating and explaining formulas so that you receive the most accurate results possible. Formula generation is more like an art than a science so you should test the results that you receive from the Formula Writer. You can insert the formula and run it, interpret the results, and then edit and resubmit the formula description if needed, to get the formula you want. You can also use the generated formula as a starting point or an idea generator for your own formula.

To get the best results from the Formula Writer:

* Include as much detail as possible in the formula description.
* Include structured references, table and column names, column/row/cell references, and so on.
* Use quotation marks around any strings (text).

h2. Formula Explanations

You can have Worksheets explain to you how a formula works. To better understand formulas in your workbook, select a cell containing a formula, then right-click and select

*Explain Formula*

.

h2. Create a Formula Using the Formula Writer

The Formula Writer enables you to describe what you want to do in a Worksheets formula and then it generates a formula that you can insert into the workbook.

To use the Formula Writer, Worksheets must be enabled for GenAI features. Additional setup steps might be required depending on your organization's subscription service agreement, and the

*Enable Worksheets GenAI Features*

option must be enabled in the

*Workday Conversation Settings*

section on the

*Edit Tenant Setup - System*

task.

h3. User-Based Security Group Membership Workflow

With this release, Workday enables you to add or remove multiple users from a single user-based security group. 

*Posted: 2024-08-07 Updated: 2024-09-18 Release 2024R2*

Setup Effort: Setup Required

Business Benefits

This ensures appropriate compliance with your security procedures, while also streamlining the process of maintaining and approving changes in group membership. All changes made using this workflow will be fully documented in the audit trail. 

 

Changes

We deliver new business processes for you to initiate changes in user-based security group membership: 

* User-Based Security Group Event for User
* User-Based Security Group Event for Group

Using the new *Update User-Based Security Group Membership* initiating action*,* you can modify the users in a user-based security group*.* You can also use the new *User-Based Security Group Event for Group* web service to initiate the User-Based Security Group Event for Group business process.

You can route these membership changes to other unconstrained security groups, for review, approval, or denial.

To ensure these tasks function as intended, we recommend disabling existing non-workflow enabled tasks using the *Disable User-Based Security Group* feature opt-in.

What's Coming Next

In 24R1, we released a business process to assign/remove multiple user-based security groups for a single user.

In 24R2, we are releasing a business process to assign/remove multiple users to/from a single user-based security group. 

In future releases, we plan to enhance the approval processes of both of these business processes. 

Additionally, non-workflow enabled tasks will be deprecated in a future release.

Deployment Considerations

* Workday recommends against using both the business process and non-workflow enabled tasks, as this could cause conflicting assignments.
* Completed events are reported in the *Find Events and Security History for User* reports. You can also create custom reports for these events using the Security History for User data source.
* Upon initiation of the business process, Workday checks to see if there are any in-progress events. If so, a message displays advising the user to complete the in-progress event before proceeding.

Seems to happen when we update the model version and it is expected behaviour.

The explanation is that updating the {{software_version}} label effectively creates a new time series: one with the old model version,  and one with the new model version. Each instance stops updating the old time series value, since each ModelSyncer trigger will happen only for new model versions , so only the _new_ time series value gets updated.Restarting the instances causes the old time series to stop  being reported and the problem goes away.

See also the discussion here [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05B5D92Y9M/p1726819697890339|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05B5D92Y9M/p1726819697890339|smart-link]

- The temporary investigative block is placed on the reported user’s account when the matter is being investigated. This block is mostly used for high and significant risk-type events (unless the process tells otherwise). This is a safety measure so the alleged bad actor cannot commit any more misconduct when using Bolt services.

- The consequential block is a result of an investigation, and in a way, it resembles a punishment for the reported user. It could be a 1-day block, 3-day block, 7-day block or even a permanent hard block. Based on the Event Confirmation and Occurrence, the Tool will suggest a consequential action for the reported user based on the Global Blocking Matrix. The Cognito tool will then suggest the consequential action. The agents must always check the SOP, as some exceptions might apply.

I’m not sure I fully understand what the issue is. In Estonia it is not possible to get notaries to “certify” random documents. They can only certify things they know to be true (e.g. registry extracts of Estonian companies). However, they will not certifyi our internal documents, the correctness of which they are not able to assess. 
Possible solutions in such events: 

# keeping notary in - instead of asking the notary to certify the document we can ask that notary certifies the signature on the document. So basically Ahto would sign and with his signature confirm the doc is true and correct AND the notary will confirm/certify that it was Ahto who signed it (again, notary will not certify the content of the document)
# dropping the notary point - Ahto as board member (or another director) certifies the document as a board member and adds his signature.

Those are the possible options so please have a chat with the client and work out an approach that suits everyone.

*Opportunity statement falls beyond the scope of RnA service.*  
The primary mission of the RnA tool is to ensure protection against potential misusage or misconfiguration that could impede business processes for valid reasons.  
While missing or ignoring RnA notifications might further slow down activities, this lies outside RnA's jurisdiction.  

Even if we were to consider integrating a notification system, the assumption about reducing the queue of pending approvals may not always hold true:  

* Individuals with a backlog of unread notifications can overlook new ones.
* Occasionally, individuals may be on annual leave.

Regarding implementation, it requires 5 man-days of effort but could potentially escalate in complexity due to configuration versatility:

* Determining the most _suitable_ retransmission frequency
** A 24-hour interval may not suffice for end-of-day requests.
** Different domains might prefer varied intervals; some tight and others more relaxed.
** Is per-request retransmission feasible?
** Does incorporating a 'Re-Send' button make sense?

We might find ourselves in situations where requesters resort to direct messaging approvers – as commonly observed today.

*_Product Comparison_*

* GitHub - Pull Requests resemble aspects seen in the *_reviewing process._*
* Once GitHub dispatches an email notification, its role concludes; monitoring approval durations falls beyond its purview.

from Privacy POV, here are the main points to have in mind before launching DQO:

* As discussed previously in [#driver-prioritization-workgroup|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C051K1C57KJ], we raised a point that DQO is a tricky feature, especially since it might fall under the scope of "automated decision making" (ADM) under GDPR.
* In short, ADM is prohibited when there's an automated decision that causes significant effect to the driver and there's no human review.
* More information on what ADM is can be found [*here*|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/4797989572/Understanding+Automated+Decision-Making+ADM].
* We did perform an analysis on whether DQO is *ADM and has significant effect:*
* From privacy POV, DQO will be a prohibited activity if it has significant effect (e.g. loss of substantial amount of earnings). If we prove there's no significant effect in the context of this specific feature - we can launch it.
* To see whether we can make this fall outside the scope of ADM, we asked the team to perform regular checks during the testing phase to see whether DQO causes the drivers to lose a significant amount of trips/earnings due to deprioritization.
* In case the test would show that the drivers lose a significant amount of money due to DQO, we shouldn't launch it in that country.
* I am not aware of the latest results per country/city, so I'd kindly ask you to check each country before launch.

We can launch in markets where tests show no significant effect, keeping it outside the scope of ADM.



I strongly suggest checking with [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] and [~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] before launching.

h2. *Initial Results From my Script*

This task seems to take less work than we initially suspected for several reasons. I’ll list my findings here.

h3. NS and SOA Records

When a route53 zone is initially created, the NS and SOA records are automatically also created. All of these currently exist outside of our Terraform state. They can be imported manually, but there is no attribute on the route53 zone resource to access these. As far as I am aware, this hasn’t been an actual problem at this point so for now the best action to take is to ignore the default NS and SOA records entirely. *This means that the zones with only the default NS and SOA records can be ignored in the scope of this task.*

h3. Domain Parking

We have a lot of empty zones because of our domain parking module. Most of these zones have no other records and the domain parking ones are in terraform so we have plenty of zones 100% in Terraform.

h3. The Actual Amount of Work Required

A total of 91 zones are entirely in Terraform according to the script, I randomly checked the zones to validate and this data seems to be correct.

The total amount of records that need to be imported to terraform is 309 - a smaller amount than I was expecting. This is across 24 zones. I would say that this is a manageable amount.

Hi [~accountid:712020:c2c173c3-935e-4969-82d9-b55800b32d30]. I have reviewed your request. 

* I have adjusted the _Check for ongoing safety investigations_ bullet point and removed the HP references from the article (/) 
* Regarding the Authority comments - I don’t think it's necessary to add instructions to not delete a user’s account if there is a comment on their profile that their data has been shared due to an authority request. It could potentially cause confusion and unnecessarily delay the account deletion.
** For more context, the Authority comments are added purely for visibility, and it does not mean that there is an open and ongoing authority case regarding the user. It just means that some of the user’s data has been shared with the authority upon request. Cases where Bolt takes any action towards a user’s account due to an authority request are very rare, and by the time the comment on the account would be left, the action would already been taken, as that happens only in very severe or business critical cases. An authority will never ask Bolt to take any action against a user. So, there is no reason to postpone deleting the user’s account just because of the informative comment on the profile. 

If anything is unclear or you still have questions, please don't hesitate to reach out, but for right now, I will be closing this ticket. 

Thank you, and have a nice day! 🙂

For your context on this topic, Jason discussed this  with the Metropolitan Police during their quarterly sync, and that’s when the question was raised - please refer to paragraph “Police report Follow-up: best practice/procedure” of this doc: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JfkSDX1tEMShz_0spXuJCEDbOpcijH0_TvyXOi7u44Y/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JfkSDX1tEMShz_0spXuJCEDbOpcijH0_TvyXOi7u44Y/edit|smart-link] 

*Current process*

_Reports concerning other incident types will receive a letter from the MPS upon conclusion. The conclusion letter will detail the outcome and the letter will be sent to the address provided in the report_ - my understanding from talking to the team is that there is a need for an address to be filled in as part of the report - and therefore we are now filling in Bolt’s (London hub) address - if the letter is sent there, doesn’t that create the same privacy issue? 

*On the topic of the driver’s address*

Drivers are required to keep their documents up to date. We collect multiple documents that include the driver’s address (DVLA, private hire licence, bank statement). Hi [~accountid:712020:0b672045-ccee-47bd-a209-1bec8346b45c] - thanks for your patience with this one. I have reviewed EY’s comments and incorporated them into the [Master DSA draft|https://docs.google.com/document/d/18k83eL5jluKdgbMlVRGRCKdk3h1WMeWvSDkQle4lMsg/edit].

In short, *the only point of disagreement between us and EY in this DSAR is in relation to clause 15* (pro-Bolt indemnity) - everything else in the DSA is aligned / finalised. EY wants to remove the indemnity wholesale, whereas we would generally push for the full indemnity to be included.

*Why is this indemnity important?*

We always push for an indemnity in our DSAs with thirds parties, as it is sensible to ensure that such agreements cover liability.
Admittedly, such indemnities are more essential for data _processor_ agreements (which this is not), where Bolt would bear the brunt of liability. Nevertheless, if EY misuses / loses / compromises the data that we are sharing with them in any way, then it is important to ensure that Bolt’s position is protected and that we will not face any knock-on liability.
The maximum financial penalties that could apply under the GDPR are EUR 20m or 4% of worldwide turnover, and so we should try and avoid limiting liability to the extent possible.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
In terms of next steps, we have three options. Let me know what you think of these:
{panel}

# *Push back and reiterate that we need the indemnity*: I have made some minor tweaks to the DSA to limit the scope of the indemnity to the personal data being processed under the DSA. We could put these to EY and reiterate that our standard position is to include this indemnity in all of our DSAs with third parties, and so we are hesitant to remove it unless EY has a clear and compelling reason for doing so. This would be the ‘best to have’ position, as it would ensure that Bolt’s position is adequately protected.
# *Accept a liability cap in the DSA*: If EY refuses to accept the indemnity as-is in the DSA (i.e., we recommend pursuing this approach in the first instance), then we could propose an indemnity cap for EY of EUR 1 million per claim. This would be an acceptable fall-back position, as some protection would still be better than nothing. If EY is amenable to this, I would be happy to prepare some wording in Clause 15.
# *Accept the current draft of the DSA, without the indemnity*: This is the least-preferred approach from the Privacy side, as it does the least to protect Bolt’s position from a contractual perspective. However, this approach has been taken with third parties in the past, even though it is not ideal. Ultimately, if EY continues to refuse any sort of indemnity, if this is the only blocker to this going forward, and if Bolt is driven to pursue this arrangement, then we can always take the business decision to go ahead without the indemnity. However, in doing so, we would have to accept the liability risk here.

Let me know what you think of the above and/or if you have any questions 🙂

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Bolt

We discussed all open topics we had during the meeting and got a green light for all of the following items:

* Licence plate angle ✅ 
* Two different tire manufacturers ✅ 
* Two different motor output power configurations on one hardware (they will re-do brake distance and ride dynamics test with both scooters, but no actual power measurement will take place) ✅ 
* Two different manufacturer batteries ✅ 

However there is one point where we fail to meet the requirements, which is the VIN-plate ❌ 


IDIADA is very strict with the VIN-plate requirements and there is no room to bend it like it was for Germany, where we managed to use a sticker instead of the plate. They require that the VIN-plate *follows the regulation precisely:*

 _Vehicles must bear the following information in a unique, permanent, legible factory marking, located in a clearly visible manner, and which does not permit reuse on another vehicle:_
_• Maximum speed_
_• Serial number or identification_
_• Certificate number → which we will receive after homologation is completed._
_• Year of manufacture_
_• Brand and model_
_The marking plate shall be made of_ *_aluminum alloy 1050 material with a thickness of 1± 0.2 mm_*_._

*_The background_* _color of such marking shall be_ *_matte black,_* _and its size shall be_ *_104x30 mm_*_, with a tolerance of_ *_± 2 mm_* _in its surface._

_The text must be printed using the laser technique and aluminum shall be used as background color._ *_The font_* _style shall be_ *_Arial bold_*_, with a_ *_height of no more than 4 mm_* _and with a tolerance of_ *_± 0.5 mm_* _in the height of the characters to be inscribed._

_The marking plate shall be_ *_fastened by rivets;_* _fastening using screws or adhesives is not allowed._



The problem is that this kind of plate will not fit on the scooter as it is today. ❌ ❌  

The location of the VIN-plate is not specified by the regulation, it can be whereever on the scooter, but it must be visible without removing any covers, which basically means we only have the underside of the diagonal tube to use.  However there is not enough room and the only way I can see to solve it is to partly cover the QR-code lasered on the diagonal tube. The space under the VIN and QR is not big enough and the distance between the VIN and QR is also too small to fit the plate. 
For future batches we should consider moving the QR-code so that we have room for the plate above the VIN, but for the already existing scooters I think there is no other way.



*Next step:* Make a drawing for the plate, get a sample, ETA and price.

* The same applies to the step for driver compensations. Compensating the driver via Beehive still means that the agent is compensating manually, so the step is not outdated. And if an agent doesn’t know how to compensate - they should check [🐝 Driver compensations in Beehive|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/71656] article. 
* I understand that it would be useful for agents to see the links to all relevant articles in processes, however, by following this logic we would also need to add links to articles such as “🌍 Issue type adding guidelines”, “🌍 Guidelines for leaving comments and internal notes” and all other articles related to certain steps, but that would make our processes overcrowded and hard to follow, so instead, we expect agents to be able to find useful articles themselves in the KB.

*How does WFM scheduling for the courses work? If you schedule a course for a specific day and time, what happens if agents don’t complete it in that time slot?*
Stefan uses Assembled to add the training to agents, and Assembled will schedule it when there is a minimum ticket volume for that day/period. If an agent misses the training in their schedule ( _I guess_) their site (_supplier_) schedules them for another time.

*Who informs the suppliers' WFM teams about the scheduling? Does this happen for every training we add to the calendar?*
Stefan creates a post on our common WFM channels (Bolt - Suppliers) and informs them that he has scheduled training for them or that they need to schedule training for them. He does this for all the training from the Calendar.

*How is Stefan handling communication with Supplier WFM teams when confirming training schedules?*
The initial plan was for me to schedule the training directly in Assembled without even asking them or communicating anything to them. I would just add them to Assembled.
I have made the decision not to do that anymore because some of the suppliers needed to understand when their agents have training. Because of that, right now, the process is that I let them know on our channels that training will be released on this date, and it must be completed by this date. The training lasts X time, and they have full control over how/when to schedule the training.

*What’s the process when there are multiple courses scheduled in the same period, and how do we ensure agents can attend without impacting quality?*
I don’t know what they mean by impacting quality. We don’t plan more than 2 hours per week, or even if we do that, over the month we don’t have more than 8 hours of training per agent.

Hi [~accountid:610279973900e60070a3495c] thanks for  looking into this one. This works for us and rest reassured that this is the standard approach/narrative used by SWEU Legal when answering authorities' data request addressed to the wrong legal entity. 

In this case we followed the suggested approach, meaning that : 

* Bolt FR replied to the authority clarifying that Bolt OPS is the entity operating the platform and asking the authority to redirect the request to Bolt OPS.
* Bolt OPS received a formal data request and replied in ENG by providing data and clarifications. The response letter was sent from the HQ email address [registry.notices@bolt.eu|mailto:registry.notices@bolt.eu] and was signed by Ahto.
* On the inspection day, FR GM clarified the respective roles. 

However, worth flagging that whilst from a contract law perspective as well as tax perspective we have grounds to assert that Bolt OPS “_holds the authority to access their information. Bolt France is not legally responsible and should not provide driver data”_ the situation from a data protection standpoint is slightly different and also local subsidiary can access data and we don’t have solid data protection arguments to push back on a data request sent to the local subsidiary. Dear Josef,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 26 August 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We attach a copy of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled, in particular your driver state logs for the period from 29 September 2023 to 30 September 2023. Please note that your time spent in the statuses ‘has_order’ and ‘waiting_orders' represent your time spent online during this period.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our privacy notice available at [https://bolt.eu/sv-se/privacy/global-privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/sv-se/privacy/global-privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

Notes for myself:

Since it is not allowed to use used e-scooters in Turkey Bolt needs to import "new" e-scooters to Turkey. For this we will use a supplier to whom we will supply used e-scooters to Aegean Free Trade Zone and they then will refurbish them and import to Turkey. We also don't want to deal with import, therefore, we will pass ownership of e-scooters. 

The ownership will pass as follows: Bolt Ops -> Cycletron (supplier of refurbishment and import service) -> Flex (local Turkish entity) -> Bolt's Turkish entity.

To regulate the refurbishment service and passing of ownership it is needed to conclude the following agreements:

* Service agreement between Bolt Ops and Cycletron for refurbishment and import ({{governing law: Estonian law}}). Draft: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/18oI4ogye3npEvxJ8xUHTzVZIhJUFhvzQ21WfDNyaugE/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/18oI4ogye3npEvxJ8xUHTzVZIhJUFhvzQ21WfDNyaugE/edit|smart-link] 
* Conditional sale agreement between Bolt Ops and Cycletron for sale of e-scooters from Bolt to Cycletron upon condition that it will: refurbish e-scooters, import them to Turkey and resell to Flex. Ownership to scooters will pass upon their delivery to Cycletron, but Bolt will be able to revoke ownership if Cycletron commits a material breach, which essentially is failure to meet conditions. This agreement will also contain a template of the sale purchase agreement that Cycletron needs to conclude with Flex. ({{governing law: Estonian law}}) Draft: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wo19l5GofBT6bFjztEvBAM2b7wBI1XkZDGRwXvMAwns/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wo19l5GofBT6bFjztEvBAM2b7wBI1XkZDGRwXvMAwns/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link] 
* Sale purchase agreement between Cycletron and Flex for the sale of e-scooters from Cycletron to Flex (with a condition to resell scooters to Bolt's Turkish entity if this is ok under Turkish law) ({{governing law: Turkish law}}) Draft: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wo19l5GofBT6bFjztEvBAM2b7wBI1XkZDGRwXvMAwns/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wo19l5GofBT6bFjztEvBAM2b7wBI1XkZDGRwXvMAwns/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link] (Annex 2)
* Sale purchase agreement between Bolt's Turkish entity and Flex for purchase of e-scooters. ({{governing law: Turkish law}})

 Bolt

* If you can see a task with an error message _Invoice sum too small_: The invoice was not generated as the driver did not owe any commission to Bolt or he had more compensation than owed commission

That’s because their commission amount is negative, meaning we don’t have any commission to invoice.

This happens when driver’s compensations/campaigns are more than their commission. Since we deduct their compensations/campaigns from their commission, in that case they don’t have any commission to invoice.

The invoice is generated once their commission again exceeds their compensation/campaign/ ride discounts sum. Then this invoice would cover the whole period without an invoice.

( as previous invoices were negative we did not issued an invoice before) 



This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducted- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.



A more detailed explanation of Netting you can be checked [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CPSiQo46UuTOCa4XmMI28Q5u3XXsaf18CQM6MM14J6Y/edit#heading=h.rmsvbaem449]

It’s typically used to support a loss of profit claim with their insurance when a vehicle is unable to operate due to an accident.

I'm not a big fan of providing such supporting letters, as we've had instances in the past where insurance claims have ended up in court. In those cases, we've been required to testify and confirm the contents of the letter. If any errors are found in the earnings calculations and we have to correct them in front of the judge, it could be perceived as documentary fraud on Bolt's part.

I would much prefer that the fleet downloads their earnings directly from the fleet platform. If that isn’t sufficient for the insurance, we can sign it to add more credibility, but that’s as far as I’d be willing to go. This approach minimizes the risk of errors in calculating the earnings.

Wdyt?

I have checked the cases and can confirm that everything looks fine on Bolts end. All of the pre-authorizations have been released to the customer. 
The user is seeing authorization and capture amounts on their bank statement. 
Some of the authorizations have been incremental authorizations. 

Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change. 

Could you please instruct the user to confirm with their bank the authorizations have been released. The users bank should be able to locate the authorizations with the amount and date. 

Some customers might not have the best visibility on when the pre-authorizations have been released. It depends on the customers bank. 

Let me know if you have any questions. 
Cheers,

        su_target_platform = pm.MutableData(name=f"signups_{target_platform}", value=train_df[f'signups_{target_platform}'], dims='obs_id')

        # Modelling counterfactual
        su_cf_platform = pm.MutableData(name=f"signups_{cf_platform}", value=train_df[f'signups_{cf_platform}'], dims='obs_id')
        beta_cf_platform = pm.Normal(name=f'beta_{cf_platform}', mu=0, sigma=50)

        #beta_trend_android = pm.Normal(name="beta_trend_android", mu=0, sigma=10, dims=('periods'))
        #beta_trend_ios = pm.Normal(name="beta_trend_ios", mu=0, sigma=10, dims=('periods'))

        #trend = pm.MutableData(name=f'trend', value=train_df['trend'].to_numpy(), dims='obs_id')

        #var_trend = pm.Deterministic(f'var_trend',beta_trend[period_idx]*trend, dims='obs_id')

        # Modelling target platform spend contribution
        vmax_target_platform =  pm.TruncatedNormal(name=f"vmax_{target_platform}", mu=priors_dict_list['vmax_mu'], sigma=priors_dict_list['vmax_sigma'], lower=0, dims=('periods', 'target_platform_channel') )

        cost_target_platform = pm.MutableData(name=f'cost_{target_platform}', value=target_platform_df.to_numpy(), dims=('obs_id','target_platform_channel') )

        contribution_target_platform = pm.Deterministic(f'contribution_{target_platform}', mm_saturation(x=cost_target_platform, vmax=vmax_target_platform[period_idx], lam=vmax_target_platform[period_idx]), dims = ('obs_id', 'target_platform_channel') )

        # Modeling counterfactual platorm spend contribution
        vmax_cf_platform = pm.TruncatedNormal(name=f"vmax_{cf_platform}", mu=700, sigma=200, lower=0, dims=('periods','cf_platform_channel') )

        cost_cf_platform = pm.MutableData(name=f'cost_{cf_platform}', value=cf_platform_df.to_numpy(), dims=('obs_id','cf_platform_channel'))

        contribution_cf_platform= pm.Deterministic(f'contribution_{cf_platform}', mm_saturation(x=cost_cf_platform, vmax=vmax_cf_platform[period_idx], lam=vmax_cf_platform[period_idx]), dims = ('obs_id', 'cf_platform_channel') )

        sigma = pm.HalfNormal(name='sigma', sigma=50)

        mu_target_platform = pm.Deterministic(f'mu_{target_platform}', 
                                              beta_cf_platform*su_cf_platform + 
                                              contribution_target_platform.sum(axis=-1) - 
                                              contribution_cf_platform.sum(axis=-1)
                                              , 
                                              dims='obs_id')
        
        pm.Normal(name=f'y_hat_{target_platform}', mu=mu_target_platform, sigma=sigma, observed=su_target_platform, dims='obs_id')

        prior_checks = pm.sample_prior_predictive(samples=500)
        print (f'\n====== PRIOR for {target_platform.upper()} model ======')
        print('Showing priors for the relevant platform only')
        print(az.summary(prior_checks, var_names=[f'vmax_{target_platform}'], filter_vars="regex", hdi_prob=0.95)[['mean', 'hdi_2.5%', 'hdi_97.5%']])
        print('\n')

        idata_ws = pm.sample(random_seed=seed, chains=4)
        #az.plot_trace(data=idata_ws, var_names=['~mu'], filter_vars="regex")

        print (f'\n====== POSTERIOR for {target_platform.upper()} model ======')
        print('Showing posteriors for the relevant platform only')
        print(az.summary(idata_ws, var_names=[f'vmax_{target_platform}',], filter_vars="regex", hdi_prob=0.95)[['mean', 'hdi_2.5%', 'hdi_97.5%']])
        print('\n')
        
        return idata_ws{noformat}

[~accountid:60b0e17e63196b00689f8d98] posting my thoughts regarding the referral codes sharing:

* As the unique referral codes can be used to identify drivers when combined with other data, these codes will be classified as personal data under GDPR. Even if they are encrypted or pseudonymized, this does not remove them from the scope of GDPR.
* This is not something that should scare us - we do have a legitimate reason to share/use these codes (encrypted or plain), and it is a better option than using direct identifiers.
* I’m not sure how the encrypted referral codes will look like - I assume they will look different but will still be tied to a specific driver.
* Encrypted or not, these codes will be considered personal data and therefore we’ll have to include them in the data sharing agreement.
* I suggest us to inform drivers that their referral codes will be shared with Edrauda (even in encrypted form) and explain how the codes will be used to speed up registration.
** We can add this info in any stage of the registration/onboarding flow, we don’t have to update the driver privacy notice for this.

Hi there [~accountid:62b2cf3c0c77011bdfdcdbcd] ,

When we receive requests from law enforcement/authorities, we evaluate whether we can lawfully disclose personal data under GDPR.

Under GDPR, we must have a valid legal basis to share data. For sharing with authorities, this usually requires a specific legal obligation.

In this case, as pointed out by [~accountid:610bac826051c5006affb87a], the legal basis cited by the inspectorate doesn’t seem to apply to us, as we are not the employer of the drivers. Therefore, it doesn’t create any legal obligation for us to share the data.

Unless local Slovakian legislation defines "employer" broadly enough to include platforms like ours, this is not a valid legal basis for disclosure. In this case, we can explain to the inspectorate that we do not act as an employer, and the drivers are not our employees, so we cannot share the requested data based on the law they provided.

If that helps, we use the following template to request for an alternative legal basis before rejecting the request (you can add the explanation that we’re not the employer):



Hi ${user_firstname},

we acknowledge your request *EDIT: Specify an ongoing document or file number*, dated *EDIT: Specify the date request received.*

Firstly, we wanted to assure you that ${brand} understands the seriousness of this request and we look to assist law enforcement whenever we are able to.

At ${brand}, we take the privacy and security of our customers, employees, and independent contractors very seriously. We only engage in data sharing with third parties where we are satisfied that the requirements of our third party data sharing policy have been met. This means that the request for data is lawful, necessary, proportionate, and limited to the specific purpose outlined in the request.

After carefully reviewing your request, we have determined that you have not provided us with a reference to the specific law or regulation that obliges ${brand} to disclose the data requested. In this instance, ${brand} will be unable to meet its legal requirements for establishing a legal basis for data disclosure.

To allow us to validate your request, we kindly advise you to provide a reference to the specific law or regulation which allows ${brand} to release this data. Providing the necessary details will enable us to properly process your request in accordance with applicable privacy laws and regulations.

+About the legal bases, we have this part on the KB:+

*Step 3. Check if we are obligated to share the data*

If any legal obligation is cited, the request must include the link or reference to the local law/provision that obligates us to assist the authorities and disclose the data only if a request meets Art. 5 GDPR requirements (data is necessary, proportionate, and limited to what is required for the specific purpose).

* Look for explicit references to legal provisions or regulations that the authority claims to rely on.
* Check this legal act or regulation is included in [*Legal Bases that oblige Bolt to share user's data*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/83887#list-of-legal-bases-applicable-in-different-countries]
** If the legal act or regulation *is included* in the list for the specific country, proceed to Step 4
** If the legal act or regulation *is not included* in the list for the specific country:
*** Confirm the existence of the mentioned legal act or regulation by searching for it on the internet.
*** Analyse the reference to the legal provision to ensure it imposes an obligation to disclose the data.

{quote}*Additional information about the link or reference to the local law*

*Note*: In some cases, the authority can provide a Court Order that obliges Bolt to disclose the data. We should not ask the authority to provide a reference to a legal basis as the Court Order itself is sufficient. In this case, review the Court Order to verify whether it specifies that Bolt should disclose the data to a specific authority and proceed to Step 5 (necessity and proportionality have already been assessed by the court).

If you’re unsure about the Court Order, escalate the case to the CS Privacy Compliance team.{quote}

* *Legal basis is complex or unclear*
** Escalate the case to the CS Privacy Compliance team and proceed according to their instructions.
* *No legal basis is provided*
** Request it using the [Legal basis is not provided in the data request|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/67379] template and put the case *_On-hold_*.
* *Authority doesn’t send the legal basis after 5 days*:
** Deny the request using the [Legal basis is not provided - rejecting the request|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/29879] template.
* *Legal basis is provided*: Proceed to step 4.







+The legal bases that we have on KB for Portugal are:+

{code:sql}SELECT
    sc.name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS orders,
    COUNT(DISTINCT IF(o.state = 'finished', o.id, NULL)) AS finished,
    COUNT(DISTINCT all_ot.id) AS all_order_tries,
    (CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT IF(o.state = 'finished', o.id, NULL)) AS DOUBLE) /
        CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS DOUBLE)) AS finish_rate,
    COUNT(DISTINCT IF(o.state = 'cancelled' AND ot.state = 'client_did_not_show', ot.id, NULL)) AS client_did_not_show,
    (CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT IF(o.state = 'cancelled' AND ot.state = 'client_did_not_show', o.id, NULL)) AS DOUBLE) /
        CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS DOUBLE)) AS client_did_not_show_rate
FROM glue.ng_public.company_order o
    JOIN glue.ng_public.company_order_try ot
        ON ot.city_id = o.city_id 
        AND ot.order_id = o.id 
        AND ot.created_date = o.created_date
        AND ot.created > date_add('minute', 30, o.created) 
        AND ot.retry_to_try IS NULL
    JOIN glue.ng_public.company_order_try all_ot
        ON all_ot.city_id = o.city_id 
        AND all_ot.order_id = o.id 
        AND all_ot.created_date = o.created_date
    JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_city sc 
        ON sc.id = o.city_id
WHERE o.created_date >= CAST('2024-09-01' AS DATE)
    AND o.type = 'sequence'
    AND o.created_by = 'client'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY finished DESC;{code}

* In any case, as mentioned before, despite of the roles of the companies, the argument to push back on the social security authority’s request based on privacy angle is very weak.

** From privacy POV, this is just a technicality and not something that prevents either of the companies to share data with the Social security authority.

Hi [~accountid:61d5747249f19500694358eb] why do we want to press charges if this person is willing to pay? 

If we proceed with pressing charges, it is unlikely we will ever be able to collect the full amount. First, it will take several months for the court to issue a judgment, followed by potentially a year before that judgment becomes final.

Additionally, during the criminal proceedings, the judge may decline to order any payments for damages, instead referring the matter to a civil court. In that scenario, it could take an extra year for the civil court to issue a final decision, after which we could enforce the judgment.

Given that this person is currently willing to repay the damages, I recommend we accept the value of the new scooter and ask them to pay that amount.

Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

Hackaton/Qualiton in Rakvere - participation in team working with project Airport Directions:[https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/RDR-1810|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/RDR-1810|smart-link] 

* One of questions that we posed for this project was to find out, what is the percentage of users, who click on Get Directions button before requesting a ride from an airport. 
* Our hypothesis was that the current Get Directions button’s design does not convince users that the button is interactive.
* I did a search in Mixpanel to find out how many users who, at the moment of confirming ride pickup location, are located in Tallinn and Heathrow airports, later tap on Get Directions button. 

My search had a couple of limitations that could affect the veracity of search results: 

# the search parameters would exclude any potential ride requests from these airports, made by users located outside of them;
# due to Mixpanel search parameters, I had to take rough coordinates of Tallinn and Heathrow airports -  while they have irregular shapes, I searched only coordinates in a shape form, closest to the whole airport polygon.

My search outcomes:

* Between August 18 - September 17, 16094 users confirmed pick-up within TLL airport polygon > only *1.65%* of them tapped on Get Directions.
* During the same period, *30017* who confirmed the pickup point within Heathrow airport polygon - *5.51%* of those tapped on Get Directions.

I later asked RiderX data analyst to check in the database if these results were accurate - and there was a mismatch between our findings. 😅 We later used the following finding from the database in our project presentation:
